## Drops this cycle (operator-mandated review — what was dropped, why it fired, why it was judged droppable)

### (a) T-1092's close-out teeth gate → issue #344

- **What**: the mechanical close-out backstop cross-checking a task's `- spec-review:` election against actual close-out behavior — a gate inside `bin/close-out.sh` plus its fixtures — carved out of T-1092's shipped scope via a class-B re-freeze (intent-hash v1→v2).
- **Why it fired (trigger + measurements)**: the spec's own pre-commitment trigger (one named component drawing an independently-new Blocker/Major across consecutive rounds) fired six times in succession against this one component: round 1 (anchor/scope Major), round 2 (boundary-asymmetry + pipefail/SIGPIPE Blockers), then — after two "final design fix" rewrites (single-normalization extraction, then CR-strip + three-way fallback disambiguation) — QA rounds 3 through 6 each independently found a **new, distinct** guard-anchor-weakness instance: internal double-whitespace in a heading, leading whitespace on an unrelated later heading defeating the boundary check (the dangerous false-PASS direction), a CRLF-terminated record defeating heading detection entirely, and finally a zero-space/U+00A0 heading invisible to both judgments at once. Six independently-reproduced defeats across six rounds, cited verbatim in `.shell-team/interventions/T-1092.md`'s own class label progression (guard-anchor-weakness ×2 → ×4 → ×5 → ×6). QA's own round-6 assessment: the two-discipline hand-rolled scan "may have hit its structural ceiling for this property."
- **Why it was judged droppable**: the axis, the spec-review mode itself, the Specify-seam gate, and the docs — the actual deliverable this task exists to ship — were never touched by any of the six defeats; every one targeted only the auxiliary mechanical backstop layered on top of an otherwise-complete feature. The receiving vessel is issue #344, which carries all six defeats **verbatim as its own requirement list** rather than a summary, so the next attempt starts from a complete, empirically-defeated design-space map instead of zero. The verification path that remains: T-1092 ships with the `spec-review` election recorded on the board and read by the orchestrator/human at freeze time — the same mechanism every other first-freeze gate in this loop already ran on before any of them had a mechanical backstop. Nothing about the axis, the mode, or the gate itself becomes unverifiable; only the redundant machine cross-check is gone, and it is gone into a tracked, requirement-seeded issue rather than into silence.

### (b) T-1094's mechanical half (`team-init --trial-branch`) → issue #348

- **What**: a `--trial-branch` flag for `bin/team-init.sh` that would create and switch to the trial branch mechanically, as issue #334's own outcome sketch described ("likely shippable as documentation plus a `team-init` flag that creates the branch").
- **Why it fired (trigger + measurements)**: dropped **at planning time**, not discovered mid-task. `pm-spec` measured, first-hand, that `bin/team-init.sh` matches the `^bin/[^/]*\.sh$` executing-surface pattern that four already-merged criteria on this same base range lock as an allow-list boundary — T-1084 AC11, T-1092 AC5, T-1092 AC16, and T-1093 AC8 — so adding a git-invoking branch there (or a companion test file, equally blocked by the `tests/` half) would turn all four red at once.
- **Why it was judged droppable**: `bin/team-init.sh` itself runs zero git commands — `grep -n -E '(^|[^[:alnum:]_])git([[:space:]]|$)' bin/team-init.sh` returns no match, measured live — so the scaffolder is branch-agnostic by construction, and `git switch -c <branch>` followed by `team-init` is already the *complete* setup procedure, missing nothing except one convenience keystroke sequence collapsed into a flag. The capability ships **whole** this sprint, as docs plus the manual two-command sequence; only the flag's syntactic sugar is deferred. The receiving vessel is issue #348, filed with the four allow-list citations as its own reason. The verification path that remains is undiminished: there was never a "mechanical" verification path for a flag that doesn't exist, and the manual route is the one `qa-verifier` actually exercised live this round (both layouts, the global-excludes remedy, teardown).
- Source: `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1094 board entry ("deferral" paragraph), issue #348.

### (c) T-1094's AC10 execution criterion → issue #348 (comment)

- **What**: AC10's original scope — a live, throwaway-git-repository EXECUTION of the documented trial-branch setup/teardown recipe, run and asserted by the criterion itself — downgraded to a static assertion of the shipped command text only.
- **Why it fired (trigger + measurements)**: the spec's own pre-commitment named AC10 as **Droppable-3rd** in its drop order *before a single review round ran*. The trigger — two consecutive rounds each landing an independently-new Major on the same named component — then actually fired: spec-review round 1 found none of the declared layout/global-excludes classes exercised at all; round 2, after a redesign, found two **new, distinct** defects — (a) an ambient `core.excludesFile` makes the documented plain `git add` abort under `bash -e` for an ordinary adopter (reproduced empirically by the reviewer against their own real global excludes), and (b) the two-arm run asserted only `--get todo`, never `--get specs`, so a regression dropping the second `git add` argument would pass both arms undetected.
- **Why it was judged droppable**: this is the case where the disposition was **pre-priced, not discovered** — because the frozen spec named AC10 Droppable-3rd before review started, executing the drop when the trigger fired required no new design judgment, only confirming the trigger's factual precondition ("at the trigger the drop is the DEFAULT... one more patch is not"). Critically, the verification did not vanish — it **moved**: both round-2 findings became binding obligations on `qa-verifier`'s own behavioral run at the train's gate instead of on AC10's own mechanism, and QA's clone run (a real throwaway `git init` scratch repo, never a clone of this repository) proved both obligations live — the documented `git add -f` remedy commits all 12 scaffolded files under an isolated `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` exclusion, and both resolved paths (`base` + `specs`) are committed in both the default and legacy layouts. AC10 itself still pins the static command-text surface a reader actually copies, so a future edit to the shipped commands still trips a checker; only the "re-run it in a fresh repo every time this one criterion is checked" duplication of QA's already-scheduled work is gone.
- Source: `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1094 board entry (pre-commitment paragraph + "pre-commitment executed — Droppable-3rd" paragraph), QA verdict (2026-08-24), issue #348.

<!-- retro-section: lessons -->
## Lesson candidates

- `[target-specific]` A hand-rolled two-discipline heading/verdict text extraction (this repo's close-out teeth gate) is not adversarially closable by iterative patching once it has already absorbed two full design-level rewrites. 状況：機械的ゲートが自由形式 markdown の見出し・判定文字列をアドホックな正規化で分類している × 継続：同一コンポーネントに対し、設計レベルの作り直しを 2 回試みた後もなお 3 件目の独立した defeat が見つかる → 行動：4 件目のパッチを試みず、pre-commitment のティース剥離ディスポジションへ直行し、既出の defeat 一覧をそのまま次 issue の要件シードにする。Source: `.shell-team/interventions/T-1092.md`, `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1092 entry.
- `[common]` A venue-gap fix scoped to "recreate this one named branch in the scratch clone" does not generalize to "recreate every branch-name literal a base-ref discriminator can name" — the same git-clone behavior (local branches survive only as remote-tracking refs) bites a second, differently-named ref in the very next round. 状況：スタック/兄弟ブランチ対応の check が `git merge-base <branch-literal> HEAD` で自身のベースを新規 `git clone` 内から読む × 継続：既に一つのリテラルを直した後、範囲内に新しい別のブランチリテラル（例：`develop` 自体）が現れる → 行動：スクラッチクローン内で check 行の FAIL を信用する前に、対象スペック／read-set 全体を base-ref discriminator の全ブランチリテラルについて grep し、それぞれを正しい SHA でローカルブランチとして再作成する。Source: `.shell-team/test-recipe.md` (T-1094 entry + rework-round entry).
- `[common]` The means-ends 4-question reflection (main value green? auxiliary component? structural disposition exists? cumulative cost vs one more round?) can resolve a loop-guard STOP with zero host escalation on its very first live firing, when a structural (not incremental) closure genuinely exists. 状況：loop-guard が STOP を返したレビューラウンドで、繰り返し発生する指摘が主要成果物ではなく補助的なコンポーネントに集中している × 継続：同種の指摘（同一コンポーネントへの≥2 回の同クラス指摘）が認識可能になった最初のラウンドで発生する → 行動：エスカレーション文を書く前に 4 問リフレクションを実行し、構造的な解消策が見つかった場合はオーケストレータ自身の常設権限で実行し、そのような解消策が見つからない場合にのみホストへエスカレーションする。Source: `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1093 loop-escape record @ `a0c3c38`, issue #346.
- `[target-specific]` Naming a task's exact drop order and trigger condition inside the FROZEN spec at authoring time — before any review round runs — converts a later mid-task design judgment call into a mechanical trigger-confirmation when it fires. 状況：spec 起筆段階で、後の実装時にアドバーサリアルに脆弱、または環境依存になり得ると事前に識別できるコンポーネントがスコープに含まれる × 継続：同種の予測可能な脆弱コンポーネントを含む将来の全タスクに適用可能 → 行動：pm-spec は起筆時点で Droppable-Nth の順序とその発火条件をフリーズ文書内に明記し、発火時にオーケストレータがゼロから処分を発明せず、発火条件の事実確認だけで実行できるようにする。Source: `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1094 entry (pre-commitment paragraph + Droppable-3rd execution).
- `[common]` Record-accuracy risk on a quantitative claim tracks a role's *exposure* to writing raw numeric literals (population counts, round tallies, byte deltas), not the role's identity or underlying model — a role whose standard output format requires transcribing such numbers will carry nearly all of a corpus's quantity-claim defects by construction. (Adjacent to an existing T-1065-era finding already surfacing in this repository's retro history — not independently cross-checked against `.shell-team/lessons.md` line ranges this round, flagged for the human to check for duplication before merging.) 状況：ある役割の標準出力フォーマットが、再実行可能なコマンドに埋め込むのではなく裸の数値リテラルを書くことを要求している × 継続：その役割がそのようなリテラルを書くたびに、サイクルを問わず再発する → 行動：「誰が何を記録するか」についてのレッスンやチェッカーを書く際は、役割の identity より先に露出（数値リテラルを書く機会の数）を重みづけし、構造的な解決策として数値をコマンドで導出させる設計（このスプリント自体が採用した `- reproduce:`/`- command:` 埋め込み型導出パターン）を優先する。Source: `capture_t1065-record-accuracy-analysis.md` (orchestrator-supplied memory input — n/a as a repository artifact).
- `[common]` (unverified this round — flagged, not fabricated) Mid-flight correction messages sent to an in-progress dispatched instance may carry a higher chance of being treated as suspected prompt injection than the same correction delivered by resuming an already-completed instance with a "verify mechanically before acting" framing. 状況：fan-out/dispatch バッチが実行中で、共有された前提を横断的に訂正する必要がある × 継続：まだ実行中のインスタンスへ訂正を届ける必要があるたびに再発しうる → 行動：この cycle の正確なインスタンス件数の一次資料が見つかるまでは lesson を確定させず、実行中への SendMessage 訂正を避け、完了済みインスタンスの resume+reframe を優先する運用を暫定的に採る。Source: n/a — could not be located in any committed artifact this round (see `## Notes`); do not merge into `.shell-team/lessons.md` without first locating a citable source.
